learning_objective: The learner will differentiate the role of each of 10 items in a model-comparison experiment as independent variable, controlled variable, measured result, or uncontrolled variable, with at least 9 of 10 correct.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** variable-role-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** differentiate
**Learning Objective:** The learner will differentiate the role of each of 10 items in a model-comparison experiment as independent variable, controlled variable, measured result, or uncontrolled variable, with at least 9 of 10 correct. **Prerequisites:** independent variable, controlled variables, uncontrolled variable, metric selection, fixed inputs (all defined in the sections above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of the 10 items the learner commits one of four roles before the sim reveals the answer. A choice is correct when it equals the Correct role column. Mastery is 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. Reading the items is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Anything that is the same in every run is controlled, whether or not it was decided. (2) A measured result can also be the independent variable. (3) A variable that cannot be controlled can be ignored. (4) The model's default setting counts as controlled. **Instructional Rationale:** Differentiating roles needs the learner to ask two questions of each item, who set it and whether it was held the same, so the items cover all four roles and include two that look controlled and are not. **Content:** The four roles the learner chooses from: "Independent variable", "Controlled variable", "Measured result", and "Uncontrolled variable". The experiment: ten candidate models each run the same three skills on one DGX unit, and the question is how well each completes them. | # | Item shown to the learner | Correct role | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Which model is loaded for the run | Independent variable | It is the one thing the experiment deliberately changes. | | 2 | The course description, an unchanged copy for every run | Controlled variable | It was held fixed on purpose. | | 3 | The harness version, pinned to one release | Controlled variable | It was held fixed on purpose. | | 4 | Wall-clock time of the stage | Measured result | It is an outcome recorded for every run. | | 5 | Which DGX unit a run happened on, when runs were spread across both with no plan | Uncontrolled variable | It varied without being decided, so a difference could belong to the unit. | | 6 | The prompt text for each stage | Controlled variable | It was held fixed on purpose. | | 7 | Number of tool calls that failed | Measured result | It is an outcome recorded for every run. | | 8 | Other work running on the machine during the run | Uncontrolled variable | It varied without being managed. | | 9 | Quantization, each model's default 4-bit file | Controlled variable | The same level was chosen for every model. | | 10 | Whether a model's reasoning mode is on, when each model uses its own default | Uncontrolled variable | It differs by model without being decided, so it is mixed with the independent variable. | **Provenance:** The items are synthetic but drawn from this evaluation's design, and the sim labels them "synthetic example". The roles come from the sections of this chapter above. **Rules:** Items are shown in the fixed order 1 to 10. Each allows one final choice, and exactly one role is correct for each. A variable is "Controlled" only if the design held it fixed on purpose, and "Uncontrolled" if it varied without being decided. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads item 1. 2. The learner chooses one of the four roles and confirms. 3. The sim shows the correct role and the Why text, and marks the item correct or incorrect. 4. The learner repeats for items 2 to 10. After item 10 the sim shows the score and the misconception behind each miss. **Feedback:** Ten items, fixed order, one confirmed choice each, no second attempt. Correct: "Correct" followed by the Why text. Incorrect: "Not quite" followed by the correct role and the Why text. The final score reads "n of 10 correct". **Starting State:** Item 1 is shown with no role chosen, and the question on screen is "What role does this play in the experiment?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter states that the model is the single independent variable, that the course description, harness version, prompts, and quantization are controlled, and that reasoning mode, context length, and server behavior were uncontrolled.
